version.changelog: Promote direct uiautomator2+RapidOCR loop (ocr_bridge.py) as primary backend after successful 12306 booking. Document Appium failure mode on WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS devices, clipboard Chinese input, virtual-list scroll unsticking.

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed Android automation bridge, but it starts persistent device-control services with weak local protections that deserve careful review before installation.

dimensions.detail: The fallback Appium path starts Appium with allow-insecure all and relaxed-security, writes screenshots and logs to predictable /tmp paths, and uses broad ADB/Appium control for connected devices.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation guidance uses a Python virtual environment and pip packages, with no hidden installer observed; the Appium startup script also launches local background services.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill openly describes generic Android app control and OCR-based booking workflows; the scope is broad but mostly disclosed to the user.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: bridge_daemon.py and start_bridge.sh create a persistent daemon and Appium session, communicate through predictable shared /tmp files without authentication or permission hardening, and may auto-start the daemon on normal commands.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The ability to read screens, take screenshots, tap, scroll, type, and change clipboard contents is coherent with the stated purpose of controlling Android apps, but it is inherently high impact.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only on a trusted, single-user machine and only when you are comfortable letting the agent see and control a connected Android device. Avoid using it during password, identity, or payment entry screens unless necessary, clear /tmp screenshots afterward, and stop Appium/the daemon when finished. The main concern is not hidden exfiltration, but overbroad persistent local control via insecure Appium settings and shared /tmp IPC.
llm.findings:
[AST4] unexpected: Starting Appium is expected for the fallback backend, but the broad insecure flags are not clearly justified or disclosed and materially increase local service risk.
[AST4] expected: ADB screenshot capture and pull are central to the OCR workflow; the unsanitized optional tag path and retained /tmp screenshots remain hygiene concerns rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
[TT2] expected: Using BRIDGE_PACKAGE to choose the controlled app fits the advertised generic bridge purpose and uses argument lists rather than shell strings, though users should understand it can target arbitrary installed apps.
[TT2] unexpected: The predictable /tmp command and response files are a real local control-channel concern because other local processes could tamper with commands or read responses.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The insecure Appium mode is not proportionate to a fallback native-app bridge without narrower feature scoping or explicit opt-in.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Shared /tmp IPC and state files are under-disclosed for a tool that can expose device UI state and issue control actions.
[SQP-2] expected: Launching automation services is expected, but the code can auto-start them and the user-facing instructions do not adequately highlight the resulting device-control exposure.
[SQP-2] expected: Full-screen capture is necessary for OCR and is disclosed, but users should treat screenshots from booking or payment flows as sensitive local data.
[SQP-2] expected: Clipboard modification is disclosed as the Chinese-input method and fits the purpose, with residual privacy and data-overwrite risk.
[RA2] expected: A persistent session is described as part of the Appium fallback design, but lack of timeout and weak IPC controls make it a review concern.
[RA2] unexpected: Running Appium persistently with broad insecure flags is not sufficiently scoped for a connected-device automation helper.
